smell_baseline_notes.smell: Cross-purposing a form control's id/ref/aria wiring onto a <Button> (judgement call, not flagged as a violation)
smell_baseline_notes.where: apps/web/components/registers/staff-advance-allocations-editor.tsx: `emptyStateProps` spreads `rowProps(0, "advance")` (an id, a focus ref, aria-invalid, aria-describedby meant for row 0's <select>) onto the empty-state "Add allocation" <Button> (#1068).
smell_baseline_notes.verdict: Not flagged as a defect. It is deliberate and narrowly scoped (only when allocations.length === 0, and only for a caller that passes rowProps at all — the register's own dialog is provably untouched), documented at length in the component's own comment and the ticket report, and driven by three dedicated tests plus two end-to-end tests proving the boundary (empty vs non-empty, with/without rowProps). Worth a reviewer's eye only because aria-invalid/aria-describedby are unusual on a plain action button, but the accessibility intent (keep the one addressable id alive so focus/scroll-to-error never targets a missing node) is sound and tested.

No ticket committed a batch of red tests before any implementation (the anti-pattern named in .claude/skills/tdd/SKILL.md).

No test reaches an internal collaborator or a private function. No mocking of anything the repo controls; grepped all four new/touched web test files for mock/jest.fn/vi.fn/spyOn and found none.

summary: Standards axis: high-quality, disciplined work across all five tickets. Migration house law (prestate/tail pins, owner/SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/ACL preservation, redo safety, immutable-migration recut convention) is followed correctly and was independently re-verified live on the lane database (all pinned shas match, all tail assertions re-run and pass). TDD vertical-slice discipline is followed throughout — no horizontal batching of tests. Tests drive public interfaces only, use independent expected-value sources, and mock nothing the repo controls. Shared files (en.json, manifest.txt, package.json's $GATES, firm-scope-db-pins corpus) are touched correctly and minimally. One minor finding: ticket #1069's own report does not document running the SWEEP-PLAN rule-(d)-required migration-pins corpus test, though independently re-running it now confirms it passes (22/22) — a reporting-completeness gap, not a code defect. The `pnpm lint` freeze-workflow failure observed during this review is environmental (origin/main advanced past this lane's base via an unrelated concurrent integration merge, PR #1140) and does not implicate any file in this lane's diff.
